title: Record job runs in an SQLite run history
description: Adds `schedule.history.RunHistory`, which records every run of the jobs passed to `track()` in an SQLite database: the job function's name, the job's tags, when the run started, how long it took in seconds, and the error if the run raised. A tracked job behaves exactly as before: its return value and exceptions pass through, and a history that cannot be written only logs an error. `table` must be a plain SQL identifier (letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit), otherwise `ScheduleValueError`. Only the newest `keep` runs of each job are kept. `runs(job=None, tag=None, limit=20)` returns the newest runs first, filtered by job name and by exact tag, and `last_success(job)` returns when the job's most recent run that did not raise started. `clock` (default `datetime.datetime.now`) gives the timestamps and durations. Includes tests.

defects.summary: The table name is checked with match() on an unanchored pattern, so any name that merely starts with an identifier passes and the rest goes into every statement as SQL.
The tag goes into the LIKE pattern unescaped, so _ and % in a tag match other tags and runs(tag=...) returns other jobs' runs.

defects.summary: The duration uses timedelta.seconds, which drops fractions of a second (and whole days), instead of total_seconds().
last_success orders by id ascending, so it returns the oldest successful run rather than the newest.

ceiling.summary: The table-name pattern uses the range A-z, which also covers [ \ ] ^ and the backtick, SQLite's identifier quote characters, so a table name that is not a plain identifier passes the check and its quoting goes into every statement.
